title: A Method for Optimal Passive Component Sizing in Phase-Shifted Pulse Width Modulated Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converters Applied to Space Robotics | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: A Method for Optimal Passive Component Sizing in Phase-Shifted Pulse Width Modulated Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converters Applied to Space Robotics | EECS at UC Berkeley A Method for Optimal Passive Component Sizing in Phase-Shifted Pulse Width Modulated Flying Capacitor Multilevel Converters Applied to Space Robotics Elisa Krause EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2025-226 December 19, 2025 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2025/EECS-2025-226.pdf High-performance, high conversion ratio power electronics are necessary to enable robotics in future space exploration. While methods have been introduced to evaluate the fundamental size of passive components in resonant-style hybrid switched-capacitor dc-dc converters, a similar large signal ripple analysis has not been done for regulating converters, specifically the flying capacitor multilevel (FCML) converter. This paper introduces a method to minimize the size of the passive components in an FCML converter in volume or mass. This technique is applied to the design of a dc-dc step-down converter for a tethered lunar robotic system. The hardware design is optimized to minimize the mass of the passive components, and a stacked printed circuit board layout is used to further reduce the size. Radiation-tolerant part equivalents are utilized to emulate the performance of a space-rated prototype, and GaN HEMTs are used to further improve the converterâs resiliency towards radiation effects. The design approach is verified through an 840 V, 600 W, 8-level FCML hardware prototype, which achieves a peak efficiency of 95.4% and a power density of 4.92 kW/kg.
